interest: This cross-reference sheet is of interest to diplomatic and legal historians studying the administration of enemy state property during World War II. It illustrates the role of Switzerland as the protecting power representing American interests in Japan, demonstrating that even at the height of hostilities in 1944, routine administrative and legal matters—such as municipal property tax assessments on U.S. government real estate in Yokohama—continued to be negotiated and tracked through neutral diplomatic channels.
overview: This file comprises a single U.S. Department of State cross-reference sheet dated March 30, 1944, indexed under decimal classifications 894.5122/2 and 894.5122/3. The sheet cross-references original communication #7725 (filed under 125.9911/326), which enclosed a note received from the Swiss Foreign Office concerning the payment of taxes on United States Government property located in Yokohama, Japan, handled via Switzerland as the protecting power during World War II.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet recording receipt of a Swiss Foreign Office communication concerning the payment of taxes on U.S. Government property in Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: A Department of State cross-reference sheet dated March 30, 1944, referencing document #7725 filed under 125.9911/326. The referenced paper transmits a note from the Swiss Foreign Office regarding tax payments assessed against U.S. Government property in Yokohama. The document illustrates the diplomatic channels maintained through Switzerland as a neutral protecting power overseeing American property interests in Japan during the Pacific War.
